assembly_notes: The root is `press_frame`, one welded CadQuery solid built as: hand arm behind the chamber, cast nose bridge ahead of it, two cast side cheeks spanning the chamber station, a transition tie block joining cheeks to arm, twin clevis lugs with rounded pin noses and a tie web, then a boolean cut of the chamber mouth (or, when the chamber flips, of its whole envelope) and a true clearance bore for the pin. The perforated chamber is its own visual on that part so a repair finding names the chamber candidate directly. `pivot_pin` is a FIXED child whose cap heads seat 0.3 mm into the lug outer faces; `lever_arm` is the single REVOLUTE child about (0, 0, pivot_z) on axis (0, -1, 0), positive q opening the arms. Every bore is shaft + 0.35 mm, so each member is carried by its joint on a running clearance and `ctx.allow_overlap` is never called. All seven chambers publish a `_Screen` (outer-face origin, outward normal, two tangents, half extents and the hole field in screen coordinates); the three screen-registered accessories are built once in that frame, which is why the same comb, ejector and liner compose with the floor screens, 001's vertical end plate and 002's front wall alike.

derived.name: span_x
derived.rationale: The chamber's own reach along the tool axis differs by candidate, so the host cannot size itself from one radius.

derived.name: cx
derived.rationale: The chamber has to clear the clevis lugs whatever its plan shape, which is 004's layout rule generalised.

derived.expression: cx + chamber_hx - 0.004, or cx + chamber_hx + 0.0007 + cradle_plate_t_m when the chamber flips
derived.name: arm_start_x
derived.rationale: The hand arm starts behind the chamber; the two cast cheeks carry the load forward past the mouth.

derived.name: rail_y
derived.rationale: Cheek station: outside the mouth cut so the welded frame stays one solid, inside the chamber wall so it welds to it.

derived.name: tail_x
derived.rationale: Total tool length follows the chamber, not a fixed constant.

derived.name: plunger_hx
derived.rationale: The face is inscribed in whichever mouth shape the chamber publishes, with a running clearance.

derived.name: plunger_hy
derived.rationale: Same rule on the second axis; it is what makes one drive fit a circle, an ellipse and a rectangle.

derived.name: engage_depth
derived.rationale: Rest engagement is capped by the cavity's own clear height so the face never reaches the screen.

derived.expression: max(open_rad, asin((chamber_top_z + 0.0065 - pivot_z) / R) - atan2(face_bottom_z - pivot_z, cx) + 0.05)
derived.name: open_travel
derived.rationale: The hinge has to turn far enough to lift the face clear of the rim, which depends on the chamber, not on the handle.

derived.name: plunger_pivot_z
derived.rationale: Every chamber puts its rim on z=0, so the pressing face's own pivot station is resolvable before the chamber is built.

derived.expression: max(lever_lift_m, pin_cap_r + 0.0038, plunger_pivot_z + hub_radius_m + 0.0034 - pivot_z for hinged drives, plunger_pivot_z + 0.0100 - pivot_z for toggle_link)
derived.name: lever_lift
derived.rationale: A drive that hangs the face on its own pivot needs the lever bar raised clear of that pivot's hardware; without this the yoke cheeks cut straight through the bar.

derived.name: screen_hole_r
derived.rationale: Two overlapping hole cylinders in the cut compound make OCC delete the whole shell, so a denser screen gets finer holes.

derived.name: cleaner_pin_r
derived.rationale: Each cleaning pin has to enter its matching perforation, so its radius follows the screen's, not a constant.

derived.name: ejector_pin_r
derived.rationale: Same registration rule for the prismatic module.

derived.name: liner_lift
derived.rationale: The liner's swing is bounded by the clear height between its own plane and the pressing face.

derived.expression: sqrt(screen_hu^2 - hinge_v^2) for a circular cavity, screen_hu * sqrt(1 - (hinge_v/screen_hv)^2) for an elliptical one, screen_hu otherwise
derived.name: liner_wall_hu
derived.rationale: A rectangular liner in a round cup has to be inscribed, or its hinge bosses land outside the wall.

multiplicities.host_capacity_expression: Both the radial and the angular pitch are floored at 2.2 mm and the hole radius is then reduced to 0.40 * min_pitch - margin (floor 0.5 mm), because two overlapping hole cylinders in the cut compound make OCC delete the entire shell. The total field is capped at 56 holes so tessellation stays inside the per-build budget; the pool's own range is 25 (004 L68-L74) to 49 (002 L98-L105), with 43 called out on 005 and 30 on both N-variants. N is capped at 7 because a 7-row field already reaches that cap on the widest trough.
multiplicities.name: screen_rows
multiplicities.spacing_expression: Row i sits at v = -hv_eff + i * (2*hv_eff/(rows-1)) with a half-pitch stagger on odd rows and a column count that follows the screen's own aspect, which is 005's 9/8/9/8/9 field (L62-L74) and perforation_grid_n30's parameterised rows x cols (L98-L119) generalised. Round footprints densify the lattice by two steps per axis because a circle throws away its corners; ribbed_cup instead lays concentric rings whose count follows each ring's circumference (round_cup_grid L70-L88).

candidates.evidence: Hollow cylindrical cup extruded from the chamber bottom to the rim, base edge filleted, hollowed by a cavity solid that runs past the rim so the top is genuinely open, then pierced by a square lattice of extrusion holes through a 3 mm floor plate. The nose is twin clevis lugs with filleted Y edges tied by a cast web ahead of the cup. Origin 003 L147-L182 adds the two features folded into this candidate: the polished collar wrapping the cup rim and a ring of radial holes low on the side wall, so the screen is not only the floor.

dimensions.hole_field: screen_rows-driven lattice, radius reduced to the field's own pitch

candidates.name: round_cup

candidates.evidence: Same round cup shell, but the hole field is concentric rings (centre hole, then rings of 6, 10, 14 at growing radii with a half-pitch angular offset) and every hole gets a wider countersink bevel cut from the floor top. A proud radial rim flange sits at the top edge with a filleted upper corner, and four radial fins embedded 2 mm into the wall stand off the outside of the barrel. Structurally distinct from round_cup in hole topology, rim profile and the added rib set.
candidates.name: ribbed_cup

parameters.name: rib_count
parameters.rationale: Radial support fins on the outside of the barrel. Pool: round_cup_grid L179 builds four at 90 degrees; the rule is index-general so 3 and 6 are the same construction.

parameters.name: rib_reach_m
parameters.rationale: How far each fin stands off the wall. Pool: round_cup_grid L176 rib_radial 0.005 with a 0.002 embed.

parameters.name: flange_proud_m

candidates.evidence: Rectangular trough: an outer box whose lower X and Y edges are filleted, hollowed by an inset box cavity, with the floor pierced by staggered rows alternating 9 and 8 holes at a constant 4.6 mm pitch. Its nose is a pair of box lugs with cylindrical rounded pin noses and one clearance bore driven through both, rather than 004's filleted plate lugs.
candidates.name: rect_trough

parameters.name: trough_aspect
parameters.rationale: Trough length over its half width. Pool: 005 L40-L41 chamber runs 0.050 long by 0.030 wide.

parameters.name: trough_fillet_m
parameters.rationale: Radius on the trough's lower edges. Pool: 005 L105 fillet 0.003.

candidates.evidence: Deep elliptical hopper: an outer ellipse extruded vertically, an inset ellipse cavity, and a staggered hole field generated conformally to the ellipse (row count from the semi-minor axis, per-row column count from the ellipse equation, 95 percent fill test). Because the rim is far higher than the flat-bar families, the upper arm grows a tall riser, a bridge and a dedicated plate bracket reaching back down into the cavity, which is the host adaptation this candidate forces.
candidates.name: oval_hopper

parameters.name: oval_aspect
parameters.rationale: Hopper semi-major over semi-minor axis. Pool: deep_oval_hopper L43-L44 RX 0.026 against RY 0.015.

parameters.name: hopper_extra_depth_m
parameters.rationale: Extra depth the oval hopper carries over the other chambers. Pool: deep_oval_hopper L45 CHAMBER_H 0.026 against the parent's 0.016, with an author check demanding > 0.020.

candidates.evidence: Lofted frustum shell: outer and inner frustums with different taper so the wall thickens downward, cut by a half-pitch staggered circular hole field, then finished with a rolled upper lip ring standing proud of the shell. The perforated bottom web is emitted as its own visual with a darker material, which is what makes the screen read as a screen instead of a cup bottom. Its nose is a cast collar plus two circular fork cheeks with polyline bridges and one bore.
candidates.name: taper_cup
candidates.notes: Emits two visuals: the tapered shell and a separately materialled perforated bottom face, which is what makes the screen read as a screen.

parameters.name: taper_ratio
parameters.rationale: Rim radius over bottom radius of the frustum shell. Pool: 006 L74 outer frustum 0.0305 -> 0.0340.

parameters.name: lip_proud_m
parameters.rationale: Radial overhang of the rolled upper lip. Pool: 006 L71-L78 rim ring 0.0352 outside a 0.0340 shell.

candidates.evidence: The only chamber in the pool whose screen is not the floor: a cylinder lying across the tool with its bore cut from the rear so a full-thickness circular end plate survives at the far face, that plate pierced by a radius-clipped square hole lattice, and the whole upper rear removed by a rounded box cut to form the loading mouth. Its nose casting is two bored knuckles plus diagonal side cheeks that leave a central lane for the plunger link.
candidates.name: drum_face
candidates.notes: The one chamber whose screen normal is not -Z. Its screen frame is the -Y end plate with u=+X and v=+Z, and the loading mouth is the box cut above z=0, so mouth_hx follows from the drum's sink depth rather than from a wall offset.

parameters.name: drum_sink_ratio
parameters.rationale: How far the drum axis sits below the rim, which is what sets the loading mouth's width. Pool: 001 L128-L142 cuts the drum open from z=-37 on a bore of radius 24.5.

parameters.name: face_thickness_m
parameters.rationale: Thickness of the circular perforated end plate. Pool: 001 L133 leaves the front 5 mm of a 54 mm drum; 006 L84 perforated face 1.2 mm.

candidates.evidence: Tapered rectangular hopper built as a ruled-off loft between two rectangles, hollowed by a second loft whose top edge deliberately exceeds the outer top so the mouth is open, and pierced by a staggered hole field driven straight through the front wall along the tool axis. Distinct from rect_trough in that the walls taper along the tool axis and the screen is the front wall, not the floor.
candidates.name: loft_hopper
candidates.notes: Screen normal is -X: the perforations go through the front wall along the tool axis, exactly as 002 drives them, and the mouth is the open top of the taper.

parameters.name: hopper_taper_ratio
parameters.rationale: Rear half width over front half width of the lofted hopper. Pool: 002 L79-L84 lofts rect(42,46) at the front to rect(34,40) at the rear.

parameters.name: hopper_front_wall_m
parameters.rationale: Thickness of the perforated front wall. Pool: 002 L79-L95 leaves 6 mm between the outer and cavity lofts at the front.

slots.name: chamber

candidates.evidence: Simplest drive in the pool: the pressing pad is a solid block cast rigidly onto the upper lever through a bridge, a stem, a riser and two side bridges, so the pad carries no joint of its own and the whole press has exactly one degree of freedom per arm. The pad footprint is sized to sit inside the basket mouth.

candidates.notes: Also carries the shared pressing-face stations used by every drive: fill ratio, thickness, rest engagement and stem width.

candidates.evidence: Also rigid on the lever, but the pressing face is a thin filleted plate carrying a full grid of 32 cylindrical pressing studs extruded downward from its underside, so the face that meets the garlic is a stud field rather than a flat block. Rest pose hovers the studs just above the chamber rim instead of burying the pad in the cavity.

parameters.name: stud_rows

parameters.name: stud_radius_m

parameters.name: stud_len_m

candidates.evidence: The plunger becomes its own part: a bored hub, a neck and a tapered frustum puck, hung on a second rivet between twin bored ears cast on the upper lever, with its own bounded revolute about the same lateral axis as the main hinge. This is the pool's self-levelling pressing face and it adds one part and one joint over the rigid families.
candidates.name: self_leveling

parameters.name: tilt_rad
parameters.rationale: Self-levelling travel either side of neutral. Pool: 006 L436-L441 limits +/-22 degrees.

parameters.name: hub_radius_m
parameters.rationale: Radius of the plunger's bored hub. Pool: 006 L229-L233 hub 0.0055 bored 0.00265.

parameters.name: puck_taper_ratio
parameters.rationale: Puck extent over the rigid face extent, i.e. how much the tilting face is undersized for its own swing. Pool: 006 L248-L251 puck frustum 0.0235 -> 0.0250 inside a 0.0258 bore.

candidates.evidence: Same separate plunger part and second revolute, but the joint is positively driven: a shaped cam disc with an eccentric lobe and a secondary lobe is unioned onto the upper lever outboard of its body on a bridge, and a hardened roller with retention end caps on an axle rides that profile from an L-bracket arm rising off the plunger hub. Distinct from self_leveling by the added cam and follower bodies and by the drive relation between them.
candidates.name: cam_follower
candidates.notes: The cam's working face is an arc concentric with the plunger pivot, so the joint's own travel opens the roller contact instead of driving the roller into the lobe.

parameters.name: cam_radius_m
parameters.rationale: Radius of the cam disc on the lever. Pool: cam_follower_plunger L355-L360 disc 0.009 with a 0.006 lobe.

parameters.name: roller_radius_m
parameters.rationale: Hardened follower roller radius. Pool: cam_follower_plunger L418-L423 roller 0.0035 with 0.0040 end caps.

parameters.name: cam_offset_y_m
parameters.rationale: Lateral station of the cam/roller plane, outboard of the lever body. Pool: cam_follower_plunger L28-L30 puts both at y = 0.016.

candidates.evidence: Four extra bodies and four extra revolutes: a yoke rocker bracket (bore boss, crossbar, diagonals, side arm plates, toggle bosses with rivet caps) pivots on the upper lever, two mirrored flat toggle links with pivot bosses and rivet caps at both ends hang from its side arms on opposed axes, and the ribbed pressing pad hangs from the rocker on a fourth pivot. Every one of them is mimic-coupled to the main squeeze pivot so the linkage is kinematically driven, not floppy.
candidates.name: toggle_link
candidates.notes: The rocker keeps 002's above-the-bar station and reaches the pressing face through two yoke side plates that straddle the lever, instead of passing through it as the source does under allow_overlap.

parameters.rationale: Length of each toggle link bar between its two pivots. Pool: compound_toggle_link L256-L263 bar 16 mm between bosses.

parameters.name: rocker_mult
parameters.rationale: Mimic multiplier from the squeeze hinge to the rocker; the links and the face are derived fractions of it. Pool: compound_toggle_link L479 uses 1.5 on a much shorter hinge range, L501/L541 use -0.7 and -1.0.

parameters.name: rocker_lift_m
parameters.rationale: How far the rocker hub sits above the lever bar. Pool: compound_toggle_link L470 pivots the rocker at z = 26 mm over a handle centred on 9.5 mm.

candidates.evidence: A cleaning insert on its own bounded revolute about a lateral axle captured in two bored bosses on a strap cast to the chamber: an axle, two short mounting arms, a rounded backing plate and a pin field whose pitch equals the chamber hole pitch and which is clipped to a circular footprint, so every pin registers with a perforation. Positive travel swings the grid clear of the screen.

parameters.name: tube_radius_m
parameters.rationale: Tube radius of both arms. Pool: 003 L60 HANDLE_R 0.006 with an author check demanding 10-16 mm across.

parameters.name: neck_len_m
parameters.rationale: Length of the cone that tapers out of the cast head into the tube. Pool: 003 L177-L182 neck cone runs 0.0345->0.0455; L232-L235 upper taper 0.028->0.044.

candidates.evidence: Both arms are four-section elliptical lofts that swell in the palm and then collapse to a 1.2 mm tip, each rotated about the lateral axis so the two arms splay apart, and the upper arm carries a slot-profile polymer grip extruded flat and rotated with the arm. Origin 006 L92-L102 and L161-L176 build the same elliptical loft and finish it with a spherical end cap instead of a point, which is the tip treatment this candidate uses so the loft never degenerates.
candidates.name: lofted_ellipse

parameters.name: palm_swell_ratio
parameters.rationale: How much the middle loft section swells over the root. Pool: 002 L120-L124 widths 18->25->24; 006 L163-L169 ellipses 8.5->14->9.8.

parameters.name: slot_grip_w_m
parameters.rationale: Width of the slot-profile polymer grip. Pool: 002 L189-L193 slot2D(151, 19).

slots.component_type: hand arm cross-section, tip and grip treatment
slots.name: arm_profile
